newsitem.title: USA: Edison, NGC push for LADWP alliance.
newsitem.headline: Edison, NGC push for LADWP alliance.

text.p: Edison International sweetened its bid for an alliance with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) on Friday by announcing a joint proposal with NGC Corp.
Under the new proposal, NGC and its power marketing arm, Electric Clearinghouse, would manage the wholesale power marketing and fuels management side of the alliance.

Edison maintains that an alliance with LADWP, which has a service territory adjoining Southern California Edison Co, would exceed the benefits of the strategic alliance the municipal utility has proposed with Duke-Louis Dreyfus.
Duke-Louis Dreyfus is a joint venture of North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp.
Bryson presented the Edison/NGC offer at a meeting of the Los Angeles City Council ad hoc committee that is reviewing possible partnerships with LADWP.
Edison noted that the selection of Duke-Louis Dreyfus was based on an evaluation of proposals submitted in a nationwide bidding process that excluded California utilities.

Edison said its three-year proposal is superior in that it guarantees more revenues to LADWP; provides more products and services to customers; provides more profit-making opportunities and makes more sense in the long-term.

The Edison/NGC offer guarantees DWP $30 million over the life of the alliance -- $20 million for wholesale marketing of LADWP's excess power, and $10 million for retail marketing of energy products and services, Edison said.

Edison said it invited NGC's participation in response to LADWP's concerns about the potential for regulatory delays. "As the largest gas marketer in North America, we will also bring unique expertise and value to LADWP's fuels management activities -- an important part of their total energy needs," said Dan Ryser, general manager of Electric Clearinghouse.
